races.name: Download The At The Races App Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Monsieur Kodi
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and a natural pace-setter on this course, he faces zero genuine pressure which makes his lead sustainable; 41 days off, but Fahey's stable has been in form (4/45 in 14 days) and he has won on Standard going before — the key question is whether the 6f trip over the shorter end of his range counts against him late.

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose recent form reads poorly (654-78) with no wins or places on similar going in his last 15 starts on AW; no headgear change and a quiet trainer yard (0/3 in 14 days) make this an unattractive profile in a race where the closers already face a structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Hierarchy
runners_data.note: Consistent AW type with three wins and five places from 11 runs on Standard going, which is the standout course-and-distance profile here; held up naturally but has the tactical nous to race prominently enough when needed, and the Osborne yard has shown a 14-day strike rate that justifies respect.

runners_data.name: Veydari
runners_data.note: A prominent racer who placed at 6f at Goodwood last time (2nd) and carries only 137lbs, giving him a manageable weight; his AW form on Standard going is thin (1 run, 2nd), but the Julie Camacho yard has been ticking over and his style places him ideally to attack Monsieur Kodi's lead in the straight.

runners_data.name: Akabusi
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse who scored at 6f on Standard going before fading to 8th last time; headgear (tb) suggests he needs an aid to maintain focus, and the AW form (8/15, 1W3P) is modest — Rob Hornby picks up the ride which provides some encouragement, but his deep draw in this pattern is a concern.

runners_data.name: King Of Chaos
runners_data.note: Landed a 6f Wolverhampton win on Standard going (1/6f/STA) within his last five runs and that course form is the sharpest angle here; operates as a hold-up horse but his Wolverhampton win shows he can travel up through the field, and at OR 72 with Marco Ghiani he looks underestimated.

runners_data.name: Twilight Madness
runners_data.note: A proven hold-up horse who is legitimately strong on Standard going (13/15 runs, 2W7P), but is mapped to midfield here because the field is saturated with closers; 91 days off is a fitness query and the 7lbs claimer Tucker has limited experience, though the horse's AW record over 6f at Wolverhampton is the best statistical fit in the race.

runners_data.name: Yachtsman
runners_data.note: Genuinely wants to race from hold-up and has done best when able to do so, but his hold-up position is unavailable in this traffic-heavy field — mapped to midfield with a STYLE_FIT flag that should temper confidence; his Limited Standard going exposure (2/9) leaves a question mark, though his 6f Goodwood win on Good shows class.

runners_data.name: Veil Of Clouds
runners_data.note: Crisford yard is in form (6/24 in 14 days) and this three-year-old ran 2nd at 6f on Standard going just 15 days ago, the freshest AW evidence in the field; a natural prominent racer, she should be able to sit just off Monsieur Kodi's back and is the most straightforwardly positioned horse in the field for this race shape.

runners_data.name: Obsidian Verse
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on Standard going (1/6f/STA) and the Fanshawe yard has been firing (5/17 in 14 days), giving this a live trainer angle; a natural hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the overcrowded rear, so she races in a compromised position and the STYLE_FIT discount applies — her win form is there but only if she can get a clear run.

runners_data.name: Nebbia
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 5f on Standard going but the step up to 6f over a wide-oval straight is untested in this going context; a true hold-up horse forced to race in midfield in this field configuration, which blunts her best profile, and the Morrison yard has been quiet (0/9 in 14 days) — each-way claims rest almost entirely on the pace collapsing late.

runners_data.name: Far Too Fizzy
runners_data.note: Showed strong AW 6f form (1/6f/STA and 3/6f/STA in last five) and the Loughnane yard is in decent nick (4/14 in 14 days); 112 days off is the major concern and she must overcome the structural hold-up disadvantage in this race shape — if she is forward enough in her work, the Standard going form makes her a genuine contender under the right scenario.

runners_data.name: Red Snapper
runners_data.note: Won at 5f and placed at 6f on Good, but Wolverhampton AW Standard going experience is absent from her record; a natural hold-up racer who is mapped to midfield in this crowded field and the inexperienced claimer (5lb) Ben Ffrench Davis adds to the execution risk — limited AW profile (hg:p) means she needs things to fall perfectly.

races.paceDynamic: Monsieur Kodi is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival willing to push him hard — he can slide into a comfortable, controlled lead from the off and dictate terms at his own rhythm over the 6f Wolverhampton straight. The bulk of the field are natural hold-up horses who will be compressed into the middle and rear, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically benefits those who can track the leader rather than those buried deep. Veil Of Clouds and Veydari are the most likely to press forward into prominent positions just off Monsieur Kodi's shoulder and represent the chief threats to his front-running dominance. This shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit within a length or two of the leader and pounce in the final furlong, rather than the numerous hold-up types who will face a stiff task making up ground against a potentially unchallenged pace-setter. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Yachtsman, Obsidian Verse, Nebbia, Far Too Fizzy, Red Snapper, and Twilight Madness are all genuine closers, but several will be forced to race in a more prominent position than is natural for them, diluting their effectiveness.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kodi Controls, Rails Run
scenarios.trigger: If Monsieur Kodi is allowed to set a comfortable, uncontested pace and the hold-up horses cannot generate momentum from deep.
scenarios.body: Monsieur Kodi bowls along in front at a sustainable clip, with Veil Of Clouds and Veydari stalking just behind; when the sprint begins in earnest inside the final 2f, those positioned prominently have first run on the closers trapped in traffic.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Monsieur Kodi's early pace is fractionally strong enough to blunt his finish but not collapse, allowing the closest trackers to pounce.
scenarios.body: Veydari or Veil Of Clouds sits within two lengths throughout and uses a superior finishing kick to reel in the leader in the final 100 yards; hold-up horses arrive too late to interfere having lost too much ground early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Monsieur Kodi is pressured earlier than expected and the pace lifts sufficiently to bring the closers into play.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-usual gallop compresses the field and opens a narrow window for the best-handicapped hold-up horses to make ground late; Far Too Fizzy and Twilight Madness, who carry strong AW form at the trip, are the chief beneficiaries of any pace collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Break, Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If there is a messy early exchange for position among the compelled mid-pack horses and the field fans wide, leaving no clear pace advantage.
scenarios.body: The race degenerates into a rough-and-tumble sprint with no single horse able to dictate, gifting an opportunity to horses who handle crowded conditions and possess tactical versatility; King Of Chaos, who won a Wolverhampton 6f last time, is best placed to exploit disorder.

watchPoints.text: Monsieur Kodi goes unchallenged in the lead — watch whether Veil Of Clouds or Veydari commit to tracking him from the first furlong, because if neither does, Monsieur Kodi could steal a match-winning advantage before the field wakes up.

King Of Chaos has the standout Wolverhampton course form (1/6f/STA) among the hold-up horses and is only 8 days since his last run — watch whether Ghiani positions him closer than his hold-up tag suggests, because that tactical flexibility has been his winning formula at this track.

Twilight Madness has exceptional Standard-going AW figures (13/15, 2W7P) but is 91 days off the track — watch the betting market for signs of stable confidence, because a fully-fit version of this horse would be among the most statistically qualified runners in the field.

The field has at least six genuine hold-up horses forced to race in midfield — watch for a wall of horses hitting the 2f pole simultaneously; jockeys who commit earliest to switching out (particularly Hornby on Akabusi and Ghiani on King Of Chaos) will have the best chance of threading through.

Veil Of Clouds (15 days since last run, Simon & Ed Crisford 6/24 in 14 days) is the most live prominent racer with recent AW evidence — watch whether Havlin elects to press Monsieur Kodi immediately or give him a length of daylight, as that positional decision will shape the entire contest.

races.name: Free Tips On attheraces.com Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Extended Credit
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo from Charles Hills with Rob Hornby aboard; unknown style leaves tactical options open and top trainer-jockey pairing makes this one of the most interesting debutants here, capable of slotting prominently if the race sets up.|

runners_data.name: One Of The Boys
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who shapes to get a dream lead; Michael Bell has a respectable 14-day record, the horse has placed twice over this course and trip on standard going, but faces the test of whether his solo lead becomes a winning one or leaves him vulnerable.|

runners_data.name: Ridger
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's 3yo has a hold-up profile and steps up from 6f at Goodwood; genuine closer who will need the fractions to be honest enough to reel in a solo leader, which is the key doubt here.|

runners_data.name: Sonbelievable
runners_data.note: Two runs both off the pace on standard and soft going with modest finishes; Joseph Parr handler is lightly represented and the hold-up style in a slowly-run race is a significant tactical concern.|

runners_data.name: Cullinan Wolf
runners_data.note: Spencer's 4yo holds up naturally and has shown a tendency to fade late; bumped to midfield on the map because the rear is congested, but this horse is unlikely to get a clean prominent pitch and the out-of-role position tempers its claims.|

runners_data.name: Rua Mor
runners_data.note: Sam England's 4yo has extensive hold-up experience over longer trips and was most recently seen over 8f; the step back to 7f on a track where he hasn't excelled makes this a tough ask, and his 46-day absence adds another layer of uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Carnival Of Light
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston sends this consistent 4yo in fair form after consecutive fourths at Goodwood over 8f; a genuine hold-up type placed in midfield on the map due to a crowded rear, and the style mismatch should temper confidence despite solid recent form.|

runners_data.name: Time Alone
runners_data.note: Debutant 3yo carrying a tongue-tie for Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole with Marco Ghiani up; complete unknown on style, but the headgear on debut is an interesting market signal and unknown profiles sometimes outrun expectations in weak maidens.|

runners_data.name: Korbut
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 3yo has the best form profile of the hold-up runners with four places from five starts and course-relevant experience on standard going at 7f; mapped to midfield due to rear congestion, but his consistent placing record makes him one of the more reliable each-way hopes.|

runners_data.name: Pink Pyjamas
runners_data.note: Jack Morland debutant with Robert Havlin in the plate; another unknown-style runner whose nature won't be known until the stalls open, though Havlin's experience ensures the horse will be placed sensibly wherever it wants to race.|

runners_data.name: Poets Praise
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3yo returns after 266 days with two modest efforts on soft ground; the long absence and soft-ground form in a standard-going contest are the headline concerns, though Beckett rarely runs horses cold.|

races.paceDynamic: One Of The Boys is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, should be allowed to dictate a sustainable, controlled gallop from the front over Wolverhampton's 7f. The hold-up brigade is unusually large — Ridger, Sonbelievable, Rua Mor, and in their true roles, Cullinan Wolf, Carnival Of Light, and Korbut — meaning a cluttered rear group will be chasing one horse who gets to write his own fractions. The field contains more hold-up types than the race map can honestly place at the rear, with Cullinan Wolf, Carnival Of Light, and Korbut redistributed into midfield slots they are unlikely to secure naturally — One Of The Boys is the only runner certain to get his preferred position. A controlled pace from the front at Wolverhampton's AW circuit, where prominent and front-running profiles regularly hold on, strongly favours horses who can track close to the single pace-setter and pounce in the straight, rather than deep closers who may find the tempo insufficient to open up the ground they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: One Of The Boys Controls
scenarios.trigger: If One Of The Boys dictates an unchallenged, measured pace and the field fails to produce a genuine sustained challenge from behind.
scenarios.body: One Of The Boys sets his own rhythm, the hold-up horses face a wall of rivals as they try to close on a well-positioned leader in the Wolverhampton straight, and a prominent or close-tracking runner lands the spoils.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly-raced or unknown-style runner settles just off the leader and quickens past at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Extended Credit, Time Alone, or Pink Pyjamas — all with unknown styles — could track One Of The Boys and prove classier when the race heats up late, with fresh legs from debutants a factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Survivor Gets Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that midfield runners travelling well conserve energy and pick up the pieces as the leader ties up.
scenarios.body: Korbut has course-relevant form on this surface and trip, and has placed multiple times at Wolverhampton's standard going; Carnival Of Light is consistent in midfield but style fit is compromised by redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If One Of The Boys goes overly fast or the pace somehow heats up dramatically and true back-markers find the gaps opening.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a genuine collapse from the front end and true hold-up horses finding clear running, both unlikely given the lone-leader setup and congested rear; Ridger or Rua Mor would be the logical beneficiaries but the race shape works against them.

watchPoints.text: One Of The Boys holds the only confirmed lead position in an 11-runner field — if he bowls along unchallenged, watch whether any of the unknown-style debutants (Extended Credit, Time Alone, Pink Pyjamas) immediately track him, as that horse may be the biggest threat.

Cullinan Wolf, Carnival Of Light, and Korbut are all genuine hold-up types crammed into a midfield map position; watch for a bunched, traffic-heavy scenario in the back half of the field where these three may block each other's runs entering the straight.

Korbut's OR of 72 versus OR=120 across the rest of the field is a stark class gap — monitor whether the market reflects hidden ability or whether this is a case of a well-placed handicapper out of his depth in a maiden.

Three debutants (Extended Credit, Time Alone, Pink Pyjamas) means the market moves at declaration time could reshape the entire race picture — any of them shortening significantly into the morning suggests stable confidence in a runner whose style is completely unmapped.

Rua Mor's last five runs are all over 8f or further including 16f trips; the drop to 7f is sharp and worth monitoring in-running to see if he finishes with purpose or simply lacks the tactical speed for the shorter trip.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Moostar
runners_data.note: In decent recent form with two seconds and a third from the last six, but her natural style is to race from well off the pace — she is shown in midfield here because there are more hold-up types than the map can place, so she may struggle to reproduce her best running style in this compressed field; the 11-day turnaround is unremarkable for this yard.

runners_data.name: Zarinca
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who sets this race's entire tactical shape; won over 6f at Wolverhampton on standard and steps up to 7f now, which looks a genuine test, but Edward Bethell's yard is firing (9 from last 34) and Dylan Hogan gets the ride with a clear brief to lead.

runners_data.name: Fizzy Cristal
runners_data.note: A two-time 6f winner at Wolverhampton on standard going, giving her strong course credentials, though this 7f trip is a step beyond anything she has won over; a hold-up operator who gets the Fahey 5lb claimer Ethan Tindall — her best chance is a run-through-traffic scenario.

runners_data.name: Court Of Stars
runners_data.note: Improved filly who has hit the frame on her last four starts including two 7f wins on standard, the most recent over this course and distance; a prominent racer who should slot comfortably into second or third behind Zarinca and represents the most straightforward threat to the leader.

runners_data.name: Eazy On The Eye
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo who has shown ability on Wolverhampton standard with a third and a second here, but the top weight of 140lbs is a significant burden in a competitive handicap; Heather Main has only 2 entries in the last 14 days (0 winners), which warrants mild caution.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Has won and twice placed over 7f at Wolverhampton on standard, making her course-and-distance record the standout factor here; she is a genuine hold-up horse who appears in midfield only because the back of the field is oversubscribed — her best form is produced when she can sit last and come with a sustained late run, which this pace dynamic may not provide.

runners_data.name: So Sassy
runners_data.note: Absent for 73 days, which is the longest layoff in the field and worth noting for fitness purposes; she wears a visor and is a genuine hold-up operator placed at midfield due to the crowded rear, meaning her natural tactics will be compromised — she has placed 11 times from 15 runs on standard going, underlining her suitability to the surface if she returns fit.

runners_data.name: Hamaleel
runners_data.note: Smart form for a 3yo on standard going — second, third and fifth over this course and distance — and her most recent effort (sixth) came over this exact trip at Wolverhampton; wears a hood, is a true hold-up type correctly placed here, and Archie Watson's quieter recent run rate (0 from 21 over 14 days) doesn't hurt if the horse is spot-on.

runners_data.name: Searchingtheblues
runners_data.note: Plenty of Wolverhampton standard experience (14 of last 15 runs) and two wins in that sample, giving her strong surface credentials; a genuine hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map as she is one of several who cannot get to the rear naturally — her recent form figures of 3-8-7-3-11 suggest she needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Show Me Gold
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance last time out to complete a sequence of four placed efforts on standard going — she arrives in form, over a track and trip she handles, and as a prominent racer she should naturally secure a good tracking position behind Zarinca; Tom Dascombe has had a quieter spell (0 from 9 last 14 days) but the horse's own form makes her hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: Lowest OR in the field at 54 but has placed in four of her last five starts and is unexposed at 7f; Grace McEntee takes the ride and the 10-day turnaround is tight but Micky Fenton runs horses regularly — a true hold-up type shown in midfield because the field is stacked with closers, so clean air and a fast finish would be prerequisites.

races.paceDynamic: Zarinca is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to press her hard from the gates, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 7f Wolverhampton standard. Court Of Stars and Show Me Gold are the other prominent-running types capable of tracking close to the pace, giving Zarinca a small group of attendants rather than a true challenger. With the tempo likely measured rather than frenetic, the race sets up as a test of those who can travel close to the pace and quicken from there, favouring prominent racers and sharp, mid-division movers who can close through a gradually-strung-out field. Five of the remaining runners — Moostar, Pickersgill, So Sassy, Searchingtheblues and Molly Mac — are genuine hold-up types crowded into the midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate them all at the rear; in truth Zarinca, Court Of Stars and Show Me Gold are the most likely to actually secure their natural forward positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zarinca Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca leads at a comfortable gallop and the pace is never meaningfully contested, allowing the front three to settle well within themselves.
scenarios.body: Zarinca dictates from the front at a steady-to-moderate tempo, with Court Of Stars and Show Me Gold tracking in her wake, and the race is decided among this leading group in the final two furlongs. Prominent racers who travel without pressure and can quicken off a measured pace are squarely in their comfort zone here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Kick Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca's tempo is genuinely slow and a wall of hold-up horses finds unobstructed runs to close powerfully in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A slow early pace compresses the field and removes Zarinca's stamina advantage, allowing the better-rated hold-up horses to reel her in late. Hamaleel and Eazy On The Eye, as genuine hold-up types with solid Wolverhampton standard form, are best placed among those off the pace to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Hots Up, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Court Of Stars or Show Me Gold applies early pressure to Zarinca and the pace becomes genuinely strong, opening the door for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop would stretch the field and drain the prominent runners before the home turn, giving hold-up types a genuine closing opportunity over the final two furlongs. Hamaleel on her best Wolverhampton form and Fizzy Cristal, a winner over course and distance, are the most credible closers in this shape — note that Moostar, Pickersgill and So Sassy are mapped to midfield but are true hold-ups who may struggle to replicate their natural style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Surprise Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded midfield causes traffic problems and an unfancied, lower-weighted runner finds a clean passage while others are baulked.
scenarios.body: With five horses compressed away from their preferred positions the midfield is likely to be congested, and a runner who threads through cleanly could steal the spoils. Molly Mac and Searchingtheblues carry the lowest weights and have the least to lose in a muddled race, though this scenario depends on fortune as much as form.

watchPoints.text: Court Of Stars and Show Me Gold could apply unexpected pressure to Zarinca early — if either tests her in the first two furlongs the predicted steady pace becomes a fast one and the entire race shape flips.

Pickersgill, Moostar, So Sassy, Searchingtheblues and Molly Mac are all genuine hold-up horses forced into a congested midfield — watch for traffic problems and interference in the straight as they all simultaneously look for gaps.
So Sassy returns after 73 days off and wears a visor — if she comes back short of peak fitness in a crowded mid-division she becomes a potential interference risk rather than a winning one.

Zarinca steps up from 6f to 7f for the first time since a seventh-place finish at Wolverhampton — if the extra furlong tests her stamina her lead could evaporate quickly in the final 150 yards, benefiting Court Of Stars directly behind.

Show Me Gold has matched or beaten every horse in this field on OR in her recent wins and arrives as the in-form prominent runner — watch how William Cox positions her in the opening furlong to gauge whether he challenges Zarinca or settles to track.

races.name: Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Go Rimbaud
runners_data.note: Has won over 8f on Polytrack standard going for John & Thady Gosden and Robert Havlin, both major positives here; returns from 83 days off but the yard's 7/16 strike rate over 14 days suggests runners come fit, and a prominent tracking role behind Brocklesby Bill plays directly to his profile.

runners_data.name: Brocklesby Bill
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner stepping up markedly in trip to 1m½f, having won over 7f at Goodwood; his headgear (hood) may assist focus in front, but sustaining the lead over this extended journey on the all-weather is a stamina question his Goodwood form over shorter doesn't fully answer.

runners_data.name: On The Inlet
runners_data.note: Comes into this race with a win over 7f standard going at Wolverhampton and solid placed form, but his natural instinct to race prominently means he arrives already squeezed out of his preferred berth — genuinely likely to race off the pace for the first time, which tempers confidence in his ability to reproduce best form here.

runners_data.name: Chapter
runners_data.note: The sole hold-up runner in the field, wearing blinkers and dropping to OR 79 for Charles Hills; his two wins came on good-to-firm and heavy ground at Hereford, and his lone all-weather start produced a seventh, making the surface a legitimate query on top of needing a strong pace to close into.

races.paceDynamic: Brocklesby Bill is the confirmed front-runner in a four-runner field and will dictate from the outset over 1m½f on the Wolverhampton Polytrack, setting a sustainable, uncontested tempo with no rival likely to challenge for the lead. Go Rimbaud and On The Inlet are both natural prominent types, but with Brocklesby Bill locked into the lead, the pace map is already full at the front — On The Inlet in particular is a genuine up-with-the-pace horse who will be squeezed into a position that doesn't suit. Chapter is the lone hold-up runner and will settle in the rear, needing the front end to tire for a late run over this extended trip. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position, with Brocklesby Bill best placed to lead and Go Rimbaud most likely to slot in just behind, leaving On The Inlet compromised. This race shape — a controlled, honest gallop from a single front-runner — most favours a horse that can race prominently in second or third and sustain its effort through the final two furlongs, making the close-up prominent profile the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Rail Win
scenarios.trigger: If Brocklesby Bill leads unchallenged and sets a steady-to-honest gallop that stretches the field without burning out.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill dictates fully from the front, rationing his effort over the extended mile-and-a-half trip, and a horse racing prominently just behind can track and pounce if the leader fades; the predictable, unsuppressed pace suits those who can settle close to the action and outstay rivals late. Go Rimbaud, having won over the standard trip at this course, is ideally placed tracking the leader in second.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Brocklesby Bill sets a fraction too fast early and the stalking horse swoops inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill's front-running effort over 1m½f proves slightly too ambitious in pace, leaving him vulnerable to being overhauled by a close-up tracker with a clean run; Go Rimbaud has the course form and fitness to capitalise from a prominent pitch. On The Inlet could theoretically benefit too but racing out of a natural role makes timing difficult.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough and sustained long enough to leave the leaders emptying inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Chapter is the only true hold-up runner here and would need a strong, relentless gallop from Brocklesby Bill to set up a meaningful closing run; the blinkered three-year-old has shown ability on good ground but this Polytrack surface produces only one data point (7th/7f/STA) and there is limited evidence to support a powerful late surge. The scenario is possible but structurally unlikely given the small field and controlled pace expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If on-pace rivals crowd Brocklesby Bill early and the race becomes a stop-start affair with no true rhythm.
scenarios.body: On The Inlet pushing forward out of its mapped position could disrupt Brocklesby Bill's lead, fragmenting the early tempo and producing a muddling race where stamina and class level the field; in a truly compressed, scrambling finish the higher-class Gosden yard horse Go Rimbaud retains residual appeal. This shape is the least likely given Brocklesby Bill's confirmed front-running role and the small runner count.

watchPoints.text: Brocklesby Bill's stamina for 1m½f is unproven — watch whether he begins to shorten his stride and tie up inside the final two furlongs, as any fade hands the race to a close-up tracker.

On The Inlet's jockey Marco Ghiani may push forward early to secure a prominent position, which could briefly pressure Brocklesby Bill and disrupt the expected controlled tempo in the first half-mile.

Go Rimbaud returns from 83 days off; watch his pre-race condition and how sharply he responds to pressure — if he is ring-rusty through the first half of the race, his chance narrows even from a good tactical position.

Chapter is the only genuine hold-up runner and will likely be last or near-last early — monitor whether the pace is truly honest enough to bring him into contention at the two-furlong pole, as in a slowly-run race he has no realistic path to victory.

runners_data.name: Scottish Anthem
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose recent form reads 53497 — the last five runs have produced no win or placing at 16f on good, and similar-going stats of 0W0P from 15 runs offer little encouragement; the 45-day absence and tongue-plate headgear add small variables but this is structurally the wrong shape for a pure closer.|

runners_data.name: Cabrera
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby takes the ride for Edward Bethell, whose T14 strike rate of 9/34 is encouraging; Cabrera is a natural prominent racer fresh off a 26-day break and a return to AW standard going where a 4th on this surface is his best recent comparable result — the step up from 12f to 14f on standard is the key question.|

runners_data.name: St Mawes

races.paceDynamic: Heathen is the one confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into an uncontested, sustainable gallop from the front over 1m6f at Wolverhampton. The pace is unlikely to be fierce — Heathen can dictate every fraction and control the tempo, which historically favours a horse that can quicken from the front or a prominent tracker who travels just off the shoulder. St Mawes and Cabrera are the natural prominent horses who can realistically sit close to Heathen in first and second place off the pace, while Arcturus Flame, Gentle Warrior, and Dance Time are all genuine front-running or prominent types who cannot all occupy those positions and have been mapped to midfield as a consequence — the most likely to actually secure a position closer to the pace are Arcturus Flame (headgear, recent run) and Gentle Warrior (consistent prominent history), with Dance Time least certain to get a forward berth. The race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers or those capable of travelling close to a solo, controlled pace-setter — pure hold-up horses are at a structural disadvantage with a sustainable gallop and a long, flat Wolverhampton straight offering little opportunity to generate the late momentum a true closer needs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Heathen Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Heathen sets an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent trackers St Mawes and Cabrera sit close enough to pounce inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Heathen dictates every fraction unchallenged, with St Mawes and Cabrera travelling just off the pace and applying pressure from the two-furlong pole; the winner comes from the front two or three as the hold-up horses are simply left with too much ground to make up. This shape strongly rewards horses who can sit handy and produce a sustained run from the front of the pack rather than a single sprint burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Heathen Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled early pace suits Heathen so well that the trackers fail to close and Heathen's stamina advantage over 1m6f proves decisive.
scenarios.body: With the gallop entirely in Heathen's hands and no rival pressing, Marco Ghiani can conserve enough energy that the horse simply sustains the effort all the way to the line; the prominent trackers fail to quicken past a horse that has dictated every yard. Though Heathen carries a STYLE_FIT flag for this race shape, the sheer lack of pace pressure makes this a genuine possibility.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Outfinish
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent horses — Arcturus Flame or Gentle Warrior — settle in midfield better than expected and produce a stronger late run than their natural style would normally allow.
scenarios.body: Forced to race off the pace against their instincts, one of Arcturus Flame or Gentle Warrior benefits from a longer-than-usual preparation and produces a sustained finish to catch tiring front-runners; this outcome is discounted because both carry STYLE_FIT flags and are racing out of their natural role. The scenario requires an unusually strong late surge from horses not bred to deliver one.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and Mersea Island or Scottish Anthem close powerfully from the back of the field.
scenarios.body: Mersea Island's strong AW form at standard-to-slow going gives it the best platform of the true hold-up types, but a sustainable Heathen-controlled pace makes this shape the hardest to execute; Scottish Anthem's recent poor form at comparable trips further reduces the likelihood. This scenario is the least probable given the structural advantages afforded to front-runners and trackers in this race shape.

watchPoints.text: St Mawes has won twice at exactly this trip on comparable going and Darragh Keenan can track Heathen directly — watch how quickly he moves to challenge in the final quarter-mile, as he is the most shape-suited horse in the field.

Mersea Island's 212-day absence is the single biggest form-book unknown — if Charlie Johnston has him primed after that layoff and the pace truly is slow, his AW record of 2W4P could make him dangerous late despite the structural disadvantage of a hold-up style.

Arcturus Flame, Gentle Warrior, and Dance Time are all naturally prominent and cannot all sit where they want — monitor the first furlong for any scramble or traffic as these three jostle for position, which could create interference or force one of them to burn energy early.

Heathen's fractional control is the race's central pivot — if Marco Ghiani elects to go very slow early to conserve energy, the closing margin for trackers narrows dramatically and Heathen's stamina becomes a bigger weapon; watch the opening half-mile splits as a guide to how the race will unfold.

runners_data.name: Special Dividend

runners_data.name: Deluded
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' runner has placed four times from seven Standard-going runs (1W4P) and holds obvious course suitability, but its genuine desire to race up with the pace will be compromised by the crowded prominent group — racing below its preferred tactical position tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Trust Amy

runners_data.name: Boy Named Sioux

runners_data.name: Espona Bay
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's runner has five placings from eleven Standard starts and is clearly effective on the surface; like the other redistributed types, its front-running instincts will be blunted by the traffic ahead, but a wide draw or early speed could allow it closer than the map suggests — low OR of 67 is still a ceiling issue.

races.paceDynamic: Special Dividend is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a ten-runner field, is likely to control this 7f Wolverhampton contest at a sustainable, metronomic tempo that rarely gets truly pressured from the front. Bone Marra, Applesandpears, and Augustus Gloop will track closely just off the leader in the prominent slots, creating a tight, bunched early group rather than a searching gallop. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Hungarian, Deluded, and Espona Bay are natural prominent racers who will be squeezed back into midfield against their instincts, further muddying the mid-race picture. A controlled, single-pace tempo strongly favours prominent hold-position types who travel within the first two or three and can produce their effort early entering the straight, rather than true hold-up horses who will need a faster pace to close.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Special Dividend Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Special Dividend gets an uncontested lead and sets a steady, metronomic tempo that saps the finishing kick of chasers.
scenarios.body: Special Dividend dictates from the front without pressure, and the prominent trackers — Bone Marra and Applesandpears — position themselves perfectly to pounce in the final two furlongs when the pace naturally quickens. Horses with strong Standard-going form in prominent positions are ideally placed to capitalise on a race that rewards those who travel economically and strike early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so sedate that multiple prominent horses quicken simultaneously off the turn, producing a tactical sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Bone Marra and Applesandpears, both proven on this surface and track configuration, are best equipped to produce a sharp turn-of-foot in a dash for the line after a dawdling early pace. Augustus Gloop's solid Standard-going record and prominent style could see him feature prominently when the finishing surge begins.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Hungarian or Deluded manages to force their way closer than their mapped position suggests, injecting unexpected pressure into the prominent group.
scenarios.body: Either horse overcoming their displaced position would tighten the race mid-pack and potentially create a stronger gallop that gives hold-up types a fighting chance of closing. Do Bronxs and Boy Named Sioux would be the chief beneficiaries if a stronger pace develops from this disruption, sweeping late into a more genuinely run contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely through the final quarter mile, leaving a clear gap for horses delivered late.
scenarios.body: Do Bronxs has shown the ability to finish from off the pace but needs a stronger-than-expected gallop to close meaningful ground in this company. Trust Amy and Boy Named Sioux are genuine hold-up types but their recent form and overall class make this scenario the least likely outcome in a race dominated by prominent-travelling types.

watchPoints.text: Watch Special Dividend's early sectionals — if Marco Ghiani is allowed to dictate unopposed at a crawl, prominent trackers Bone Marra and Applesandpears will be travelling dangerously well into the final two furlongs with no racing room concerns.

Hungarian, Deluded, and Espona Bay are all natural prominent types mapped to midfield — monitor the first furlong for any of them forcing their way forward, as three horses fighting for position could inject unexpected tempo and change the race shape entirely.

Augustus Gloop is returning from 135 days off and all his form is at 6f on Standard going — the step up to 7f after a long break makes his early pace judgment critical; James Fanshawe runners can be fit fresh but this is a significant ask on return.

Do Bronxs wears a pacemaker and has no Standard-going form — in a race where the pace is likely to be controlled and moderate, its hold-up profile needs more pace than this field appears set to generate; watch to see if Laura Pearson angles for a position closer than expected.

Bone Marra is the only runner with a confirmed recent win at Wolverhampton over today's course and distance on Standard going — if it jumps cleanly and takes up its natural prominent position without incident, it sets the form benchmark for the field.
